data.narrative:
Enfabrica, a Series C-stage semiconductor company, is valued within a comp universe of 3 public players (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private peers spanning chips and frontier silicon. The target has raised $311.1M to date across its funding rounds.

Two valuation methods are applicable. Stage-progression analysis uses the $311M total raised as a proxy base and applies a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical of Series C advancement, implying $529M. Peer-median triangulation draws from four same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables: Tenstorrent ($2.7B, Series D), Nearfield Instruments ($1.6B, Series D), Positron AI ($1.0B, Series B), and DEEPX ($529M, Series C). The peer median across this set is $1.3B, with a range of $529M to $2.7B. Public-comp anchoring via price-to-sales multiples (18.9x median across semiconductors) cannot be applied due to absence of target revenue disclosure, typical for private companies.

The two applicable methods triangulate to a valuation range of $450M (low) to $1.5B (high), with a median point of $914M. The dispersion reflects stage and revenue-profile uncertainty; the stage-progression method anchors conservatively on deployed capital, while peer-median weights comparable funding outcomes in the same sector. Key uncertainties include Enfabrica's revenue trajectory, IP differentiation relative to the peer set, and nearness to Series D fundraising.
